name: SFFT library (ETH Zurich optimized sparse FFT, versions 1-3)
workload: Discrete Fourier transform of a signal whose spectrum has only k non-zero frequencies out of n (sparse spectrum), compared in the underlying sFFT work against a full dense FFT such as FFTW; this repository itself contains no benchmark.
claimed_speedup: No numbers anywhere in the repository or its docs. The docs call it a 'high-performance C++ implementation' of sFFT v1, v2 and v3 with SSE kernels. The underlying MIT sFFT algorithm is billed as faster than FFTW for sparse spectra (Hacker News thread 'The faster-than-fast Fourier transform'), but those figures were not opened this session.
tradeoffs: Only helps when the spectrum is sparse; it is not a general dense FFT. README states it is experimental and 'NOT intended to be used as a drop-in replacement for the FFT library of your choice'. Docs say v1 and v2 work only with a few specific input parameters and v3 cannot handle noisy signals. Targets x86 with SSE; Intel IPP is required by default (configure --without-ipp disables it). It calls FFTW internally for its sub-transforms (FFTW plan flags are a plan parameter), so FFTW is a dependency as well as the baseline. GPL-2.0-or-later (strong copyleft).
caveats: Tier D: I found no benchmark numbers in the README, CHANGELOG or doc/*.rst (all read via raw.githubusercontent.com). The speedups presumably live in the ETH master thesis by J. Schumacher (2013, supervised by M. Pueschel) and the MIT sFFT papers; spiral.net, groups.csail.mit.edu and arXiv are egress-blocked, so none were opened. The claim concerns sparse versus dense transforms, so it is valid only for sparse signals. Notability is modest by stars (69) but the sFFT algorithm is widely cited; included as the single tier D for this run. Repository last updated 2015-06-03; its first commit imports 'Official download of version 0.1.0' from spiral.net, so it is not a GitHub fork. Related sparse-FFT repos mpsft and Auto-MPFT are already catalogued. The MIT original code (groups.csail.mit.edu/netmit/sFFT) was not reachable and has no GitHub canonical repo that I opened.
found_via: Hacker News: WebSearch (allowed_domains news.ycombinator.com) 'Show HN faster FFT library than FFTW' surfaced the thread 'The faster-than-fast Fourier transform' (item 3480016); the repo came from WebSearch 'sFFT sparse Fourier transform MIT code github faster than FFTW'. The HN thread itself could not be opened (egress-blocked).
